subject: Obtaining the fixed covariate effects in a autoregressive model of order 1 with covariates (AR1C)

messages.author: e9ab831d77228443
messages.subject: Obtaining the fixed covariate effects in a autoregressive model of order 1 with covariates (AR1C)
parts:
Hi INLA group,

I am trying to implemnt ar1c model, I meet some problem to include covariates in the model. I use AirPassengers data as examples (see book "Bayesian inference with INLA") .

data(AirPassengers)

##here I contain two addtional covariates x1, x2
airp.data <- data.frame(airp = as.vector(AirPassengers),
                        month = as.factor(rep(1:12, 12)), 
                        year = as.factor(rep(1949:1960, each = 12)),
                        ID = 1:length(AirPassengers),
                        x1<- rnorm(144, 2,1),
                        x2<- rbinom(144, 10, 0.2))

names(airp.data)[5]<- "x1"

names(airp.data)[6]<- "x2"

Z <- model.matrix (~ 0 + year + x1 + x2, data = airp.data)

Q.beta <- Diagonal(14, 0.001)

airp.ar1c <- inla(log(AirPassengers) ~ 1 + f(ID, model = "ar1c",
                                             args.ar1c = list(Z = Z, Q.beta = Q.beta)),
                  control.family = list(hyper = list(prec = list(param = c(1, 0.2)))),
                  data = airp.data,
                  verbose = T,
                  control.predictor = list(compute = TRUE))

summary(airp.ar1c)

Here, the summary does not report any fixed covariate effects, only an intercept.
To obatain the results of covariate effects, I try the following command, 

airp.ar1c$summary.random$ID[n+1:ncol(Z),]

Wether this obatins the correct fixed covariate estimates?

Thans in advance.
Charles

messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Obtaining the fixed covariate effects in a autoregressive model of order 1 with covariates (AR1C)
parts: Hi,

Here, the summary does not report any fixed covariate effects, only an intercept.
To obatain the results of covariate effects, I try the following command, 

airp.ar1c$summary.random$ID[n+1:ncol(Z),]

Wether this obatins the correct fixed covariate estimates?

Yes. I believe so. If you plot the posterior means you will notice that the last 14 entries do not ‘match’ the scale of the the first 144. So you will have the 144 estimates of the random effects plus 14 estimates of the fixed covariates in the ar(1) latent effect. I checked in the documentation and this is documented therein (see attached plot).

Best,

Virgilio

messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Obtaining the fixed covariate effects in a autoregressive model of order 1 with covariates (AR1C)
parts: Hi,
> Thank you for your reply. This is the same to the slm model to obtain its covariate estimates.
Yes. The estimates of the coefficients of the covariates are at the end of the random effects summary.

> Further, how to extend this ar1c to panel data setting?
> For example, I have N=100 observations and T=10 period, with a sum of 1000 observations. Should I specify a 1:1000 ID number?

I would have the spatial index with repeated values as needed, and then the panel index with repeated values as well. This is probably the simplest solution. If you want to have spatial and panel interaction… then that’s another story that will required another specification, I believe.

Best,

Virgilio

messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Obtaining the fixed covariate effects in a autoregressive model of order 1 with covariates (AR1C)
parts: Got it.
>I would have the spatial index with repeated values as needed, and then the panel index with repeated values as well. This is probably the simplest solution.

It works.

If I understand well, for a dynamic model with both a spatial lag on the dependent variable and a temporal lag on the dependent variable (no interaction of the two components) with the specification:

y_{it}=\lambdaWy_{it}  +  \rho y_{it-1} + x_{it}\beta + \eta_{i}+\epsilon_{it}

\eta_{i}  \sim iid (0, \sigma_{i})
\epsilon_{it} \sim iid(0, sigma_{it})

W is a block diagonal matrix.

We can contain a "slm" random effect component and a "ar1c" random effect component to fit this model, like

slmm1 <- inla( ln.CMEDV ~ -1 + CRIM + ZN + INDUS + CHAS + NOX2+ RM2 + AGE +
                 ln.DIS + ln.RAD + TAX + PTRATIO + B + ln.LSTAT + 
                 f(idx, model="slm",
                   args.slm=list( rho.min = rho.min, rho.max = rho.max, W=W, X=mmatrix, Q.beta=Q.beta.spatial),
                   hyper=hyper) +
                    f(It, model = "ar1c",
                                             args.ar1c = list(Z =  mmatrix , Q.beta = Q.beta.temporal)),
               data=boston.c, family="gaussian",
               verbose=T,
               control.family = list(hyper=zero.variance),
               control.compute=list(dic=TRUE, cpo=TRUE)
)

messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Obtaining the fixed covariate effects in a autoregressive model of order 1 with covariates (AR1C)
parts: Hi,

> If I understand well, for a dynamic model with both a spatial lag on the dependent variable and a temporal lag on the dependent variable (no interaction of the two components) with the specification:
>
> y_{it}=\lambdaWy_{it} + \rho y_{it-1} + x_{it}\beta + \eta_{i}+\epsilon_{it}
> \eta_{i} \sim iid (0, \sigma_{i})
> \epsilon_{it} \sim iid(0, sigma_{it})

That model is equivalent to

y_{it} = (I - \lambdaW)^{-1} ( \rho y_{it-1} + x_{it}\beta + \eta_{i}+\epsilon_{it})

Hence, you have too many terms on the right hand side that the ’slm’ latent effect does not include. In particular, the term on y_{it-1} may be difficult to handle in INLA due to the structure it imposes on the models that it can fit. Please, define your model as

y_{it} = …

So that the right hand side does not depend on y_{it}. This will give you a better sense on the model that you are trying to fit and see if ti can be fit with INLA.

Best,

Virgilio
